variables.claim_asserts: The vast majority of the simple binary-operator axiom systems illustrated by Wolfram allow operators of many forms.
variables.test_measures: The fraction of a newly generated 4,692-system family of single equations with at least three non-isomorphic three-element models.

modality.note: Finite-model enumeration is the right modality for counting operator forms, but the population and model sizes used for the decisive fraction do not reproduce the illustrated population.

assumptions.note: The verdict assumes an assessor-defined family, defines 'many' as at least three k=3 models and 'vast majority' as 80%, and counts systems with no nontrivial model in the denominator; these choices are not supplied by the quote.

scope.claim_scope: Simple equational axiom systems for a single binary operator, specifically the systems represented in Wolfram's pictures.
scope.test_scope: Canonical single equations with one to four operator occurrences, exact k=2 and k=3 models, plus incomplete capped k=4 searches.

reasons: The decisive 0.4049 fraction is calculated over a generated family not established as the family behind pages 804-805; 32.5% of that family has no k=2 or k=3 nontrivial model.
Wolfram's pictured systems include four-element operator forms, but the primary criterion uses only classes_k3; the S2 k=4 search is incomplete for 1,703 systems.

Adding found k=4 forms and excluding degenerate systems changes the many-forms fraction to 0.5198 and the single-form fraction to 0.0641, showing that denominator and model-size choices drive the refutation.
The closer supplementary Wolfram lhs==a family contains 67 of 101 systems with at least three forms at some k<=4, but 91 k=4 searches are incomplete; it cannot sustain the main-family refutation.
what_would_change_it: Enumerate the exact axiom systems shown or defined by Wolfram, complete the same element sizes shown in the source (including k=4), and derive 'many' and 'vast majority' from the source rather than fixed 3-model and 80% thresholds.
